Read a variable as a tidy data frame

Source: R/connection.R
dbReadTable-XarrayConnection-character-method.Rd

The rendering is the tidy long form of ds[name], exactly as to_dataframe().reset_index() gives it: one row per cell, every coordinate as a column. This materializes the variable, so it is guarded: reads above max_cells cells error unless force = TRUE. Set options(xrdbi.max_cells = ) to taste.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'XarrayConnection,character'
dbReadTable(
  conn,
  name,
  ...,
  max_cells = getOption("xrdbi.max_cells", 1e+07),
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

conn

an XarrayConnection

name

a variable name

...

unused

max_cells

guard threshold, default getOption("xrdbi.max_cells", 1e7)

force

bypass the guard

Value

a data frame, one row per cell of the variable

See also

tbl() or a statement (XarrayResult) to read part of a variable; the guard's option in xrdbi-package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## needs a Python environment with xarray (see ?xrdbi)
f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/trmm.nc", package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)
dbReadTable(con, "latitude")
head(dbReadTable(con, "pcp"))
## the guard: 1600 cells is over a limit of 100
try(dbReadTable(con, "pcp", max_cells = 100))
} # }
